Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Overall, vitamin D concentrations in late pregnancy were not associated with risk of postpartum depression.
Sentence: "Overall, we found no association between vitamin D concentrations and risk of PPD (p = 0.08)."
Measured as: postpartum depression (PPD)
Population: Women in the Danish National Birth Cohort: 605 with postpartum depression and 875 controls
Intervention: Late pregnancy serum 25[OH]D3 concentration (measured, not given)
Comparator: Women with vitamin D concentrations of 50-79 nmol/L
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 1,480
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Patients with depressive disorder had decreased vitamin D levels compared with healthy controls.
Sentence: "The patients with DD had elevated TXB levels and decreased vitamin D levels, as compared to healthy controls."
Measured as: depressive disorder (vs healthy controls)
Population: Children and adolescents with depressive disorder and healthy controls
Intervention: Baseline vitamin D level (observational comparison)
Comparator: Healthy controls
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 58
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
